name: pidfd_open
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_pidfd_open, pid_t pid, unsigned int flags);
Note: glibc provides no wrapper for pidfd_open(), necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: The pidfd_open() system call creates a file descriptor that refers to the process with the specified PID. It sets the close-on-exec flag and supports optional flags like PIDFD_NONBLOCK for nonblocking behavior.

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: The PID of the process to refer to.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to modify behavior, such as PIDFD_NONBLOCK for returning a nonblocking file descriptor.

return_value.success: Returns a file descriptor (a nonnegative integer)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached.
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached.
The anonymous inode filesystem is not available in this kernel.
The process specified by pid does not exist.

examples: static int pidfd_open(pid_t pid, unsigned int flags) { return syscall(SYS_pidfd_open, pid, flags); }
struct pollfd pollfd; pollfd.fd = pidfd; pollfd.events = POLLIN;
